label: token right after a d in the first two original positions
explanation: Fires during the original phase at steps t=1 and t=2 when the previous input was d, i.e. on the token that follows a d at original position 0 or 1. The current token does not matter. It is strongest (near max, about 2.6) at t=1, right after a sequence-initial d, and weaker (about 0.45-0.9 of max) at t=2 after a d in position 1. It essentially never fires after a d later in the sequence (t>=3 gives a few hundred weak activations), never at the delimiter, and almost never in the copy phase (41 activations).

issues: Minor magnitude wording: at t=2 the feature reaches up to about 0.93 of max (e.g. 's d [i:0.93] o'), not just 0.45-0.9. Average activation per step at t=2 is about 0.71 of t=1 (mass 0.415 over 16688 steps vs 0.583 over 16601), so 'weaker at t=2' still holds.

The remaining test misses (622 steps, 0.2% of activation mass) are all low-magnitude cases at t=3 after a d at position 2. The explanation already reports these, so they are not an unexplained systematic class. Including t=3 drops precision to 0.68 (test F1 0.809), so the t<=2 cutoff is justified.
The 41 copy-phase activations sit at recall_idx 1-2 and carry about 0 mass. This matches 'almost never in the copy phase'.

The other claims check out: no activations at the delimiter or at t=0; activation is independent of the current token (in_tok is flat at about 1.1x lift); test precision is 1.0 with 0 false positives; test F1 is 0.991.
